page: Microsoft Azure F2-1ams_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famsv7 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The configuration features 1 physical core and 1 vCPU, with no hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per core. The processor includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for advanced vector instructions such as AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance due to the single-vCPU limitation. The server achieves top-tier results in single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression tasks, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3743.89 and gzip compression reaching 38.98 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and database operations fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is average, measuring 42.75 GB/sec for read operations and 32.15 GB/sec for write operations. Large-model LLM inference is limited, though small 135M parameter models achieve average speeds of 176.95 tokens/sec for text generation.

This server does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring external premium storage attachments for data persistence. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F2-1ams_v7 offers a high density of memory relative to its single-core compute allocation, making it a specialized option for workloads that require a large memory footprint but do not demand parallel multi-threaded processing. Suitable workloads include single-threaded memory-intensive applications, lightweight caching layers, small-scale memory-resident databases, and basic single-threaded data processing tasks.
